templates.pattern: A man walks into a bar and asks for water. The bartender pulls out a gun. The man says thank you and leaves. Why?
templates.explanation: The man had hiccups. Bartender scared him (curing hiccups). He thanked him and left

templates.pattern: A woman shoots her husband, drowns him, hangs him, but they go to dinner together. How?
templates.explanation: She's a photographer: shoots photo, develops in water (drowns), hangs to dry

templates.pattern: What has keys but no locks, space but no room, you can enter but can't go inside?
templates.explanation: A keyboard has keys, spacebar, and enter key but none of the physical versions

templates.pattern: A man pushes his car to a hotel and tells the owner he's bankrupt. Why?
templates.explanation: He's playing Monopoly. Landed on hotel property and can't pay

templates.pattern: What gets wetter as it dries?
templates.explanation: A towel gets wetter as it dries you off

templates.pattern: Romeo and Juliet are found dead on the floor with water and glass around them. What happened?
templates.explanation: Romeo and Juliet are fish. Their bowl broke and they died

templates.pattern: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What is it?
templates.explanation: Footsteps - the more steps you take, the more footprints you leave

templates.pattern: A man dies of thirst in his own home. Why?
templates.explanation: Power was out, pipes frozen. He couldn't access water despite being home

templates.pattern: What can travel around the world while staying in a corner?
templates.explanation: A postage stamp stays in the corner of an envelope but travels worldwide

templates.pattern: A man lives on the 15th floor. Every day he takes elevator down. Going up, he stops at 7th and walks. Why?
templates.explanation: He's short/child. Can only reach 7th floor button. Walks rest of the way

templates.pattern: What has a head and tail but no body?
templates.explanation: A coin has heads and tails sides but no body

templates.pattern: A man looks at a painting and says 'Brothers and sisters I have none, but that man's father is my father's son.' Who is in painting?
templates.explanation: My father's son = me. That man's father = me. So painting shows his son

templates.pattern: Forward I'm heavy, backward I'm not. What am I?
templates.explanation: The word 'ton' forward is heavy. Backward spells 'not' which isn't heavy

templates.pattern: A doctor and boy are fishing. Boy is doctor's son but doctor isn't boy's father. How?
templates.explanation: The doctor is the boy's mother. Common lateral thinking about assumptions

templates.pattern: What breaks when you say it?
templates.explanation: Silence breaks when you speak

templates.pattern: A man wearing all black walks down a dark street. Car with lights off comes but stops in time. How did driver see him?
templates.explanation: It was daytime. Dark street doesn't mean nighttime

templates.pattern: What belongs to you but others use it more?
templates.explanation: Your name belongs to you, but other people use it more than you do

templates.pattern: A man is found dead in a phone booth with multiple stab wounds. Phone is off hook. What happened?
templates.explanation: Stabbed with icicle which melted. Water puddle remained. Classic lateral puzzle

templates.pattern: What can run but never walks, has mouth but never talks, has bed but never sleeps?
templates.explanation: A river runs, has a mouth (where it meets ocean), has a riverbed

templates.pattern: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. They catch 3 fish, one each. How?
templates.explanation: Grandfather, father, and son = 2 fathers (grandfather & father) and 2 sons (father & son)

templates.pattern: What gets bigger the more you take away?
templates.explanation: A hole gets bigger as you remove more material

templates.pattern: A man goes out in heavy rain with no protection but not a hair on his head gets wet. How?
templates.explanation: He has no hair, so no hair gets wet

templates.pattern: What has 13 hearts but no other organs?
templates.explanation: A standard deck has 13 hearts (the suit)

templates.pattern: A woman gave birth to two sons on same hour of same day of same year but they're not twins. How?
templates.explanation: They are part of triplets (or more). Not twins but born same time

templates.pattern: What occurs once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
templates.explanation: The letter 'M' appears once in 'minute', twice in 'moment', zero times in 'thousand years'
